stem: Meera keeps a potted money plant in her kitchen garden. She fixes a wide-mouthed bottle containing potassium hydroxide pellets over one half of a destarched leaf, while the other half stays outside in the open air. After keeping the plant in sunlight for 6 hours, she tests the leaf with iodine solution. Only the half outside the bottle turns blue-black. What does this experiment show?

options.text: Potassium hydroxide helps the leaf to prepare starch
Sunlight alone is enough for the leaf to prepare starch
Carbon dioxide from the air is essential for the plant to prepare starch
The half-leaf inside the bottle produced more starch than the half outside

teacher.key_rationale: Potassium hydroxide absorbs carbon dioxide inside the bottle, so the enclosed half-leaf lacks carbon dioxide and forms no starch (no blue-black colour). The half in open air has carbon dioxide and forms starch (blue-black). The only difference is carbon dioxide availability, so the experiment shows carbon dioxide from air is essential for starch preparation. Key: C.
